name: Google Antigravity

deny.note: Structurally mode-independent: a PreToolUse hook returning decision 'deny' hard-blocks, traced in the shipped binary.

ask.note: The strongest ask semantics of any agent surveyed. TWO ask verdicts: a plain `ask`, which honours a cached 'Always allow' and so can be silently satisfied, and a `force_ask` that cannot be suppressed by a prior always-allow. No other agent here ships a non-suppressible ask.

onCrash.note: Undocumented — the public docs, the shipped hooks.md and the SDK reference all omit it. Established by reading the binary.

interception.note: Unusually broad. Matcher names are derived mechanically from an internal step-type enum of roughly 115 values.

canModifyInput.note: The shipped local docs describe input rewriting; the public web docs list only decision/reason/permission and are incomplete here.

exposesMode.note: No permission-mode field. Read from the embedded FileDescriptorProto rather than inferred from the prose docs.

modes.askSurvivesNote: force_ask survives everything, which is why the mode is not needed to decide whether an ask will land.

upstreamLimitations: Fails open and silently on crash, deletion or timeout: it logs and proceeds.
A plain `ask` is satisfied by a cached 'Always allow', so only force_ask is a guaranteed prompt.

Hook config is workspace-scoped at <repo>/.agents/hooks.json, discovered by walking up from cwd. A repository can therefore ship hook configuration, which is a supply-chain surface LeastGrant's threat model does not currently cover.
CustomizationConfig carries a switch that can disable the hook engine, and LeastGrant has no way to express 'installed but switched off at the host'.
leastgrantLimitations: No adapter ships yet. This file records a completed evaluation.
If an adapter is written, force_ask is the primitive that should back an abstract ASK, and it must be exposed as a capability rather than hardcoded by agent name.
